name: Commit Tracker
author: LizinDev
description: GitHub-style daily commit activity in the bar, with a history panel, streaks and links to your commits

barWidget.description: One box per day for the last few days, shaded by how much you committed. Left click opens a contribution graph with streaks, a repository filter and your commits (click one to open it on GitHub); right click opens the settings.

schema.label: Folders to scan
schema.description: Where to look for git repositories: a JSON array or a comma-separated list of paths.

schema.label: Scan depth
schema.description: How many folder levels below each scan folder to search for repositories.

schema.label: Authors
schema.description: Emails or names to count (exact, case-insensitive), as a JSON array or comma-separated list. Empty uses your git user.email and user.name.

schema.label: Intensity by
schema.description: Shade boxes by commit count or by lines changed.

schema.label: Intensity levels
schema.description: default shades at 1, 2, 4 and 8 commits (1, 50, 200 and 800 lines); or give four ascending lower bounds such as 1,3,6,10.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: Safety-net poll. Local commits refresh within seconds through a file watcher.

schema.label: Colors
schema.description: theme follows the Omarchy theme; github uses GitHub's green contribution colors.

schema.label: Theme color
schema.description: With theme colors: a theme role (accent, foreground, urgent, muted) or a hex color.
